static_traits.name: Li Danna
static_traits.medical_history: without similar problem history;not yet received psychotherapy;No major physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, organized; able to recall and quantify experiences (such as rating activity enjoyment); highly cooperative, willing to try restructuring thoughts; Low mood, describing 'emptiness' 'sadness'; negative automatic thoughts such as 'what is the point' 'will not get better' in thinking; Neutral attitude.

basic_info.main_problem: I have been feeling extremely depressed, and even paddleboarding, which I used to love, no longer brings any joy. This depression began about six months ago; although I tried to keep participating in activities that used to bring joy, symptoms gradually worsened, and I cannot find a specific cause.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this depression severely affects my quality of life and my enjoyment of activities I once liked.

core_beliefs: I cannot get joy from anything

special_situations.event: Trying paddleboarding, an activity once loved no longer brings joy
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an activity cannot make me feel better immediately, it is meaningless; this shows I will not get better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces self to keep trying paddleboarding, hoping repeated participation will bring back the joy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What is the point? This will not make me feel better

special_situations.event: Over the past six months, still feels bored when participating in other previously enjoyed leisure activities (watching movies, reading)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If even activities I once loved no longer make me happy, it means nothing can make me happy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Participates reluctantly but is emotionally detached, hard to engage
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Nothing can make me happy anymore

special_situations.event: When considering whether to share his depressive feelings with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express depression, they will not understand and will only tell me to 'get better quickly', which will make me feel worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids sharing the true extent in depth, keeping silent and bearing it alone

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and accepted, to be able to experience joy and vitality again
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being brushed off or negated (being told to 'get better quickly'), thus aggravating pain and Loneliness
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being negated or hurt by keeping Silence and not disclosing

object_relations.self_representation: A Loneliness person not understood, feeling empty
object_relations.object_representation: Bystanders who may look down on one or demand one 'cheer up'

manifestations: Describing 'meaninglessness' 'emptiness' 'sadness' when participating in paddleboarding, movies, reading, etc.
Activities once loved now bring 'no joy at all', experience markedly declined (8–9 points down to 1–2 points)
Depression has lasted six months; hard to gain a sense of meaning from daily life
outcomes: Lowered participation and engagement, Decreased quality of life

manifestations: Having several close friends but not yet sharing the true extent of depression
Choosing not to disclose for fear friends will not understand or tell oneself to 'get better quickly'
outcomes: Social support hard to take effect, increased subjective Loneliness

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self; that is, the individual redirects the energy originally meant to be sent outward back toward the self, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language expressions include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it' and 'I should not trouble others'.
manifestations: Not expressing the true extent of depression to friends, choosing Silence and bearing it alone
Seeks less outside help, swallows pain inward

positive_force: Still tries to participate in activities (tried paddleboarding multiple times in the past six months)
Willing to seek professional help and cooperate with cognitive restructuring exercises
Has a certain self-observation and quantification ability (able to recall and rate past and present pleasure levels)
Has some social support resources (a few friends he can confide in)
negative_force: Depressive mood persists and broadly affects interest and pleasure
Obvious cognitive biases (overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, negative predictions about the future)
Avoidance of external support and non-disclosure, leading to The support system has difficulty functioning
Treating current negative emotions as objective facts (emotional reasoning), further Reinforcement of Meaninglessness

target_behavior.behavior: Anhedonia and negative predictions appear when participating in once-loved leisure activities (such as paddleboarding, watching movies, reading)
antecedent: When preparing or planning to join leisure activities
target_behavior.core_reason: Six months of persistent depression accompanied by cognitive biases (overgeneralization, all-or-nothing thinking, emotional reasoning), taking the present sense of emptiness as fact and making negative predictions about the effects of activities
target_behavior.function: Avoiding disappointment and discomfort, lowering investment to avoid re-confirming the 'Meaninglessness' experience
target_behavior.consequence: Quality of life markedly declines, interest and pleasure disappear or markedly decrease, and socializing and daily life are affected
